claims.text: The initial catalyst is a nanoparticulate, equimolar PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution.
Increasing Pt content by approximately 5–10% relative to the equimolar composition shifts the d-band center of active sites.
The proposed d-band-center shift enhances ethanol oxidation activity.
The proposed d-band-center shift enhances selectivity during ethanol oxidation.
Slight Pt enrichment changes the electronic neighborhood of active sites.
Changing the active-site electronic structure modifies the adsorption energies of ethanol and its intermediates.
The modified adsorption energies enhance electron-transfer kinetics.
The modified adsorption energies promote more complete ethanol oxidation, including oxidation to CO2.
Pt enrichment can improve activity and complete-oxidation selectivity without compromising durability.
Under the specified electrochemical conditions, Pt-rich catalysts will have higher ethanol-oxidation current densities than the equimolar baseline.
Under the specified electrochemical conditions, Pt-rich catalysts will have greater selectivity toward complete oxidation products, including increased CO2 formation, than the equimolar baseline.
The hypothesis is restricted to nanoscale catalysts with confirmed homogeneous solid-solution alloying and no significant phase segregation.
The proposed operating range is 0.1 M ethanol in 0.5 M H2SO4 at 60–70 °C and 0.0–1.0 V versus RHE.
Pt enrichment may cause phase separation or segregation that introduces effects beyond the intended d-band-center shift.
